sentences.text:
In pursuance to the same, Mr.
Pradeep Khandelwal had executed an agreement to sale dated 22 nd May 2019 with Mr. Nagendra Mishra for the sale of aforesaid lands along with other lands and Rs.1 crore was also received in the Axis Bank account of Mr. Pradeep Khandelwal in installments.

He next submits that the aforesaid lands were jointly owned by the applicants and complainant and due to typographical error, Mr. Pradeep Khandelwal had executed the agreements to sale dated 22nd May 2019 in respect of the complainant's share in aforesaid land.
It is also submitted that Mr. Pradeep Khandelwal soon realized the error and executed another agreement to sale dated 7 th August 2020 excluding the share of the complainant in aforesaid land.
But the complainant without realizing the change/correction in agreement to sell for aforesaid lands had filed the complaint with the respondent wherein the FIR was registered.

He also submits that the applicants are ready to furnish adequate security and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Court, therefore, the present applicants may be granted ad-interim temporary bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the application for ad-interim bail.

After hearing counsel for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, in particular, the quality of the evidence, the applicants are 56 & 50 years of age and the co-accused have already been granted ad-interim bail by this Court vide order dated 24.01.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.(A) No. 104/2023, this Court is of the considered opinion that it is a fit case to grant ad-interim anticipatory bail to the applicants.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 01/2023 is allowed.

It is directed that the applicants shall be released on ad-interim bail on their furnishing a personal bond in sum of Rs.50,000/- each with one surety in like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned Arresting/Investigating Officer or the concerned trial Court.
